message.abstract: <jats:p>Service organizations increasingly require decision-support systems that move beyond risk prediction toward resource-feasible intervention prioritization. This study proposes an explainable predictive prescriptive multi-objective decision analytics framework integrating leakage-controlled temporal modelling, probability calibration, explainable machine learning, resource-capacity representation, and Pareto based optimization. The framework was evaluated on 118,219 valid service cases using chronologically separated training, model-selection, calibration, and locked-test periods. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM were compared, with LightGBM providing the most balanced locked-test performance (ROC-AUC = 0.640, PR-AUC = 0.323, F1 = 0.413, MCC = 0.171). Isotonic regression was selected for probability calibration, while TreeSHAP identified temporal context, service characteristics, recent demand, geographic factors, and workload relative to capacity as the principal risk drivers, with highly stable global rankings across bootstrap resamples. The prescriptive layer formulated intervention prioritization as an exact ε-constraint 0-1 multi-objective optimization problem. Across nominal capacity scenarios of 5-30%, maximum calibrated risk coverage increased from 42.91% to 82.76%, while ideal point compromise policies achieved 24.46-66.40% coverage using substantially less than the corresponding capacity ceilings. Matched-budget evaluation showed that the Pareto policy outperformed most baseline allocation strategies, although the Risk or Burden-ratio heuristic closely reproduced the selected compromise solutions. Sensitivity analysis across Q75, Q80, and Q90 delay definitions showed stable ROC-AUC values despite substantial prevalence shifts, and an external Prefix-2 benchmark supported predictive transferability. The framework provides a transparent bridge from calibrated perspective risk estimation to explainable, resource-constrained intervention decision making.</jats:p>
title: An Explainable Predictive-Prescriptive Analytics Framework for Resource-Constrained Service Intervention Decisions
